title: Ext of a finite locally free module
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\mathcal F$ a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module,
with $\operatorname{Ext}$ as in [def-sc-ext-sheaf] and
$\mathcal F^{\vee}=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal O_X)$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms

$$
\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\;\cong\;
\mathrm H^i\bigl(X,\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}
\mathcal G\bigr)\qquad(i\geq0),
$$

in particular
$\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal O_X,\mathcal G)=\mathrm H^i(X,\mathcal G)$.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ext-evaluation], naturally in $\mathcal G$, evaluation identifies $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ with $\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes\mathcal G$. The global-sections clause of [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifies its sections on $X$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$. By [def-sc-ext-sheaf] and [pqf-def-cohomology], this gives the degree-zero isomorphism.

On each $V_a$ of an open cover with $\mathcal F|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$, the definition of sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] gives $\mathcal F^{\vee}|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$ by taking the Hom of a finite direct sum. Thus the dual satisfies the same finite locally free open-cover condition (compare [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]), and [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact] makes $T(-)=\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes-$ exact. By [lem-sc-ext-evaluation] and the global-sections clause of [def-pur-sheaf-hom], $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,-)\cong\Gamma(X,T(-))$. Kernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so evaluating at $X$ preserves kernels and finite products; hence $\Gamma(X,-)$ is left exact in the sense of [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

The tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-adjunction], with its tensor factors interchanged using the sectionwise symmetry [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm] and sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], makes $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)$ right adjoint to $\mathcal F\otimes-$. The evaluation isomorphism [lem-sc-ext-evaluation] identifies this right adjoint with $T$; [def-pur-sheaf-hom] specifies the sheaf Hom involved. The functor $\mathcal F\otimes-$ is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact], so [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] makes $T(I)$ injective for every injective $I$. The injective resolution concentrated in degree zero shows $R^i\Gamma(X,T(I))=0$ for $i>0$ by [def-sp-left-exact-additive], hence $T(I)$ is $\Gamma$-acyclic by [def-sp-acyclic].

By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives, so both the source and target of $T$ meet the hypothesis of [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite]. Apply that node to $\Gamma(X,-)\circ T$. Its $i$-th right derived functor is $\mathrm H^i(X,\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes\mathcal G)$ by [pqf-def-cohomology], while [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] identifies the right derived functor of $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,-)$ in the second variable with $\operatorname{Ext}^i_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ (correcting the contravariant wording in [def-sc-ext-sheaf]).

For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, [def-pur-sheaf-hom] identifies its dual with $\mathcal O_X$, and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] identifies $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G$; the isomorphism above specializes to the stated formula.
